title: WHERE EXACTLY IS THE OBSERVER?
goal: Look for the observer's exact boundary and notice that every candidate location is itself observed.
steps:
1. Search Carefully — Search carefully for the boundary, size, and location of the one who observes.
2. Check Behind — Check behind the eyes, chest, head, and surrounding field.
3. Observe Found — Every found sensation is itself observed.
4. Rest Inability — Rest with the inability to locate a final point.
win: Eyes, head, chest, and surrounding field supplied sensations but no final point that could be identified as the watcher.
supports:
• Notice resentment as a warning; offer only genuine options.
• Offer alternatives only if genuine; state consequences clearly.
• Protect your capacity; delay your answer.
• Use a short no; repeat the same wording calmly.
• Let guilt pass; keep the limit simple.

safety:
PAUSE
Do not continue if location inquiry provokes feeling unreal or detached from yourself.

title: PUT THE COMMENTATOR IN THE CHEAP SEAT
goal: Use real task feedback while letting self-commentary remain faint and unanswered at the edge.
steps:
1. Choose Skill — Choose one familiar, low-risk task with clear external feedback.
2. Centre Feedback — Put sight, touch, sound, or the work result in the centre of attention.
3. Demote Voice — When self-commentary appears, let it continue faintly at the edge without answering or silencing it.
4. Finish Unit — Finish one complete task unit using feedback—not self-opinion—to make corrections.
win: One work unit was corrected from sight, touch, sound, or result rather than from inner opinion.
supports:
• Park secondary tasks; keep one task visible.
• Close what you do not need; reduce nearby noise.
• Put the phone out of reach; use one screen.
• Use a short focus block; return after interruptions.
• Use one window at a time; take a short break.
formula_flow: Choose Skill → Centre Feedback → Demote Voice → Finish Unit
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if divided attention reduces accuracy or makes the activity unsafe.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PLAY EMOTION JENGA
goal: Remove one emotion temporarily to learn what it was contributing, then restore the whole stack.
steps:
1. Name Stack — Name two or three feelings and place each on a separate mental block.
2. Pull One — Temporarily bracket one block with the phrase ‘not deleted—just outside this test.’
3. Check Remainder — Observe what changes in the remainder: body location, urge, story, intensity, or nothing at all. Keep one difference.
4. Rebuild Stack — Restore the removed block. Repeat only if useful, then rebuild the complete stack before finishing.
win: One feeling was bracketed without deletion, revealing a change in body, urge, story, intensity, or nothing at all.
supports:
• Avoid bargaining with the urge; remember urges peak and fall.
• Use your hands; delay ten minutes.
• Delay acting for ten minutes; tell someone early.
• Change rooms if possible; drink some water.
• Avoid bargaining; make access less convenient.
formula_flow: Name Stack → Pull One → Check Remainder → Rebuild Stack
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if the game causes numbness, feeling unreal or disconnected, suppression, or pressure to erase a valid feeling.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: REMEMBER THE FUTURE IN ADVANCE
goal: Imagine the scene just after completion, then trace backward to the first movement you can do now.
steps:
1. Create Memory — Create a memory-like scene set just after completing the action.
2. Include Time — Include time, location, body posture, one sensory cue, along with what you did when difficulty appeared.
3. Look Backward — Look backward from that imagined completion to the first real movement and do it now.
win: A future memory supplied posture, sensory detail, and a coping response that led directly back to a real first action.
supports:
• Feel your feet; return to one real sound.
• Slow your physical pace; keep eyes open.
• Keep your eyes on something steady; hear one real sound.
• Notice three colours; look around the room.
• Notice room temperature; feel both feet.
formula_flow: Create Memory → Include Time → Look Backward
safety:
PAUSE
Keep future scenes realistic rather than using fantasy as avoidance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: INTERVIEW THE OBSTACLE
goal: Ask the obstacle what it is protecting and negotiate one step that respects the valid need.
steps:
1. Give Obstacle — Give the obstacle a character and ask three questions: What are you protecting.
2. Ask Fear — What do you fear will happen.
3. Make Step — What would make one step acceptable.
4. Picture Negotiate — Picture its answers, then negotiate a small action that protects the valid need without handing over total control.
win: Fear, protection, and conditions for movement became explicit enough to make a small agreement possible.
supports:
• Start smaller; make it visible.
• Do the easiest useful part; set a two-minute timer.
• Choose tiny action; prepare first.
• Open only what you need; start with one minute.
• Touch the first item; open the task.
formula_flow: Give Obstacle → Ask Fear → Make Step → Picture Negotiate
safety:
PAUSE
Do not personify intrusive voices or experiences if that worsens symptoms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: IMAGINE THE INNER MACHINE
goal: Map the full trigger-to-result loop and change one link instead of fighting the whole system.
steps:
1. Imagine The Parts — Imagine the trigger, meaning, physical feeling, urge, action, result, and feedback.
2. See The Links — Imagine how each part affects the next and where the loop returns.
3. Find the Lever — Notice one place where a small change may shift the whole loop.
4. Test It — Try that small change once.
win: A single point in the sequence shifted once, creating fresh evidence about how the larger pattern responds.
supports:
• Eat if hungry; move away from the cue.
• Avoid bargaining with the urge; tell someone early.
• Make access less convenient; drink some water.
• Eat or drink if hunger matters; delay ten minutes.
• Do one incompatible activity; keep your hands busy.
formula_flow: Imagine The Parts → See The Links → Find the Lever → Test It
safety:
PAUSE
Keep the mental picture simple. Stop if you begin analysing without taking action.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: OPEN THREE ENDING ROOMS
goal: Compare three possible endings at the decision point, then choose the one best supported by evidence and values.
steps:
1. Identify Critical — Spot the critical decision point in the dominant future scene.
2. Create Endings — Create three endings by changing the choice there: cautious, courageous, and collaborative.
3. Cost — Notice the cost and value of each.
4. Keep Best — Keep the ending that best fits evidence and values.
win: Cautious, courageous, and collaborative endings showed different costs before one path earned the next move.
supports:
• Pick one value for this decision; accept the trade-off.
• Name what matters today; remove one conflicting commitment.
• Check whose goal you are chasing; remove one conflict.
• Keep meaning practical; choose aligned action.
• Name today's value; protect important time.

safety:
PAUSE
Do not imagine unsafe endings merely to increase variety.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CHANGE THE SYMBOL’S JOB
goal: Change one feature of the symbol carrying the state, then turn any inner shift into action.
steps:
1. Choose Symbol — Imagine one symbol that represents the state.
2. Change One Property — Open it, cool it, soften it, widen it, or give it an edge.
3. Notice Response — Notice what changes inside as the symbol changes.
4. Translate — Turn that inner shift into one practical next move.
win: The symbol softened, opened, cooled, widened, or gained an edge, and one practical move followed the change.
supports:
• Add small friction; use the same replacement repeatedly.
• Make the new habit easier; reduce easy access to triggers.
• Delay the routine; change one cue.
• Remove easy access; interrupt the sequence.
• Replace one response; expect slips and restart quickly.

safety:
PAUSE
End the exercise when imagery grows disturbing, bizarre, or detached from reality.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

goal: Find the inner camera angle that keeps the facts intact while giving you more choice.
steps:
1. Adjust — Adjust the internal scene’s distance, height, direction, and frame one at a time.
2. Test Far — Test close, far, eye-level, above, behind, wide, and cropped.

win: Distance, height, direction, or framing changed without changing the event itself, and one view increased present agency.

• Reset without self-criticism; expect slips and restart quickly.
• Reduce easy access to triggers; delay the routine.
• Notice the trigger; remove easy access.

title: BORROW ONE MOVE FROM THE AVATAR
goal: Borrow one useful behaviour from an imagined capable figure without trying to become them.
steps:
1. Create Figure — Create a figure who represents the needed capacity—steady, playful, discerning, brave.
2. Give Posture — Give it posture, voice, and one signature behaviour.
3. Borrow One Move — Borrow only that behaviour for this situation. You do not need to become the character.
win: A steady, playful, discerning, or brave action was used once while the rest of your identity stayed yours.
supports:
• Stay somewhere physically safe; keep movements gentle.
• Sit somewhere safe; unclench your jaw.
• Stop body scanning; reduce caffeine.
• Reduce extra stimulation; keep your body supported.
• Wait out the surge; sip water if it helps.

safety:
PAUSE

title: FOUR-CELL DECISION MATRIX
goal: Compare options across values, downside, reversibility, and learning instead of trusting one total score.

win: The pattern across four criteria made a containable-risk option easier to recognise.

title: WHICH REGRET ARE YOU AVOIDING?
goal: Compare the regrets of acting, waiting, doing nothing, and betraying what matters.
steps:
1. Estimate Regret — For each option, estimate regret of action, inaction, delay, and self-betrayal.
2. Describe Future — Say the future scene behind the highest score.
3. Ask Regret — Ask which regret is reversible and which conflicts most with your values.
win: The most important future regret became clearer, including whether it could be repaired later.
supports:
• Use one priority; remove one conflicting commitment.
• Keep the action small; accept the trade-off.
• Choose aligned action; make the next hour reflect it.
• Keep meaning practical; check whose goal you are chasing.
• Review the cost; pick one value for this decision.

safety:
PAUSE
Do not let imagined regret override present safety or evidence.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT
goal: Compare two options at a time using one declared criterion and let the survivor earn the next look.
steps:
1. Seed Options — Picture the available options into a simple bracket. Give an unpaired option a bye rather than inventing a rival.
2. Pick Criterion — Choose one criterion that matters for this round and picture it above the bracket. Do not switch it mid-game.
3. Play Pairs — Compare only two options at a time. Advance the one that better meets the declared criterion.
4. Crown Next — Crown the final survivor as the next option to inspect or act on—not as a permanent life verdict.
win: The bracket produced a next option to inspect without pretending the winner was a permanent life verdict.
supports:
• Notice the trigger; change the environment first.
• Make the new habit easier; delay the routine.
• Remove easy access; change one cue.
• Change the environment; expect slips and restart quickly.
• Move the cue; interrupt the sequence.
formula_flow: Seed Options → Pick Criterion → Play Pairs → Crown Next
safety:
PAUSE
For high-stakes choices, use the winner only as the next research step and include qualified advice and all safety criteria.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: REMOVE WHAT THE CHOICE WOULD ‘PROVE’
goal: Remove what each option would supposedly prove about you before comparing the real consequences.
steps:
1. Say About — Name what each option would supposedly say about you—successful, loyal, brave, weak, ordinary.
2. Drop Labels — Mentally remove those identity messages from the decision.
3. Check Again — Re-check only consequences, values, constraints, and evidence.
4. Notice Shift — Notice whether the preferred option changes.
win: Status labels such as brave, weak, loyal, or successful stopped influencing the choice unless they carried actual evidence.
supports:
• Name what matters today; remove one conflict.
• Use one priority; review the cost.
• Protect important time; check whose goal you are chasing.
• Check whose goal; act before motivation.
• Make the next hour reflect it; name today's value.

safety:
PAUSE
Identity and community may be legitimate values; distinguish them from performance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE PAST INVESTMENT GETS NO NEW VOTE
goal: Ignore what is already spent and compare the choices only from today forward.
steps:
1. Hide Already — Hide what has already been spent.
2. Compare Options — Compare options from today forward using remaining cost, likely benefit, opportunity cost, and risk.
3. Remove Sunk Vote — Reveal the past investment afterward only for learning, never for sharing.
win: Remaining cost, likely benefit, opportunity cost, and risk chose the next move while past investment stayed a lesson.
supports:
• Ask what would change your mind; question absolute words.
• Delay the verdict; check another angle.
• Ask what else could fit; test the assumption.
• Check the whole situation; notice absolute words like always.
• Use recent, concrete evidence; check the base rate.

safety:
PAUSE

PLAY TIME
45–60 seconds

GOAL
Ignore what is already spent and compare the choices only from today forward.

HOW TO PLAY
1. Hide Already — Hide what has already been spent.

3. Remove Sunk Vote — Reveal the past investment afterward only for learning, never for sharing.

WIN
Remaining cost, likely benefit, opportunity cost, and risk chose the next move while past investment stayed a lesson.

• Check the whole situation; notice absolute words like always.
• Use recent, concrete evidence; check the base rate.

title: WHOSE HANDWRITING IS ON THIS BELIEF?
goal: Trace the belief to who taught or rewarded it, then decide whether you still want to carry it.
steps:
1. Name Modelled — Name who modelled, rewarded, enforced, or normalised the belief.
2. Picture Original — Picture the original context and what compliance protected.
3. Ask Whether — Now check if current-you endorses it under present values and data.
win: The original context and protection became visible, then current values and evidence got a separate vote.
supports:
• Look for one missing fact; delay the verdict.
• Check the base rate; add the missing context.
• Use current facts; notice absolute words like always.
• Question absolute words; delay major conclusions when upset.
• Separate guess from evidence; use a real example.

title: MOVE THE RULE BETWEEN WORLDS
goal: Move one inherited rule across different settings and keep only what remains ethical and workable.
steps:
1. State Rule — Picture the rule without naming who taught it.
2. Change Context — Place it in three contrasting settings—for example family, workplace, and friendship—with different power and consequences.
3. Compare Effects — Compare who is protected, restricted, or harmed in each setting.
4. Keep Core — Keep only the part that remains ethical and workable across contexts; notice the rest as conditional.
win: The rule changed meaning across family, work, and friendship, revealing which parts were universal and which depended on context.
supports:
• Check the whole situation; use a real example.
• Delay major conclusions when upset; use current facts.
• Check another angle; ask what would change your mind.
• Check what you actually know; separate possibility from probability.
• Question absolute words; avoid treating guesses as facts.
formula_flow: State Rule → Change Context → Compare Effects → Keep Core
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if the comparison turns into contempt for people or excuses unsafe or unlawful behaviour.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

BREAK THE EXPECTED SEQUENCE

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

GOAL
Test one respectful alternative to an expected life sequence without attacking the whole culture around it.

HOW TO PLAY
1. Picture Culturally — Picture the culturally expected next step.
2. Name Benefits — Name who benefits, what value it serves, and what it costs you.
3. Generate — Generate one respectful alternative sequence.
4. Test Small — Test a small part without declaring war on the whole culture.

WIN
Who benefits, what the norm serves, and what it costs you became visible before one small alternative was tried.

• Avoid treating guesses as facts; question absolute words.
• Test the assumption; delay the verdict.
• Use a real example; check the whole situation.
• Check what you actually know; separate guess from evidence.
• Check another angle; use recent, concrete evidence.

MIND BEND
Tradition can contain value and pressure at the same time. Changing one step does not require rejecting every part of the sequence.

FORMULA FLOW
Picture Culturally → Name Benefits → Generate → Test Small

SAFETY
PAUSE
Consider relationship and safety consequences, especially in restrictive environments.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: HIDE THE CROWD’S ANSWER
goal: Form your own quality judgment before looking at ratings, likes, rankings, or social consensus.
steps:
1. Group Preference — Before seeing ratings, likes, rankings, or group preference, assess quality using your own criteria.
2. Hold Judgement — Hold the judgement and reasons.
3. View Crowd — Reveal social proof afterward and change your view only if the crowd supplies new evidence, not mere numbers.
win: Your criteria and reasons existed before social proof appeared, so numbers could add evidence without replacing judgment.
supports:
• Separate possibility from probability; use a real example.
• Notice absolute words like always; use current facts.
• Check the whole situation; use recent, concrete evidence.
• Question absolute words; ask what else could fit.
• Ask what would disprove it; delay major conclusions when upset.

safety:
PAUSE

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RETURN THE SHAME TO ITS OLD ADDRESS
goal: Keep any repair that truly belongs to you and return inherited contempt or impossible standards to their source.
steps:
1. Identify Whose — Spot whose rule the shame is enforcing and the setting where it was learned.
2. Ask Whether — Check whether you still endorse that standard.
3. Keep Repair — Keep any ethical repair that is truly yours; return contempt, prejudice, or impossible expectation to its source.
win: The old rule was identified, current endorsement was checked, and shame lost the parts that were never ethically yours.
supports:
• Avoid global words like always; prefer repair.
• Separate guilt from responsibility; describe the behaviour, not yourself.
• Keep guilt precise; do not punish yourself for learning.
• Avoid global labels; name the behaviour.
• Recall capability; make repair smaller than self-punishment.
formula_flow: Identify Whose → Ask Whether → Keep Repair
safety:
PAUSE
Seek support when shame is severe, trauma-linked, or tied to self-harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE
goal: Shrink a broad belief until it states where, when, and with whom it actually fits.
steps:
1. Name The Belief — Say the belief silently.
2. Imagine Four Limits — Think about when, where, with whom, and under what conditions it may be true.
3. Test Inside — Picture one real case where it fits.
4. Test Outside — Picture one real case where the belief does not fit.
5. Shrink the Rule — Say a smaller, more accurate version of the belief.
win: One fitting case and one exception produced a smaller statement that was more accurate than the original rule.
supports:
• Repeat without arguing; keep the limit simple.
• Take time before saying yes; repeat the same wording calmly.
• Use a short no; keep consequences realistic.
• State consequences clearly; delay your answer.
• Offer only genuine options; use one clear sentence.
formula_flow: Name The Belief → Imagine Four Limits → Test Inside → Test Outside → Shrink the Rule
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use belief boundaries to minimise abuse, discrimination, medical facts, legal duties, or immediate danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

PLAY TIME
60–90 seconds

GOAL
Shrink a broad belief until it states where, when, and with whom it actually fits.

HOW TO PLAY
1. Name The Belief — Say the belief silently.
2. Imagine Four Limits — Think about when, where, with whom, and under what conditions it may be true.
3. Test Inside — Picture one real case where it fits.
4. Test Outside — Picture one real case where the belief does not fit.
5. Shrink the Rule — Say a smaller, more accurate version of the belief.

WIN
One fitting case and one exception produced a smaller statement that was more accurate than the original rule.

• Repeat without arguing; keep the limit simple.
• Take time before saying yes; repeat the same wording calmly.
• Use a short no; keep consequences realistic.
• State consequences clearly; delay your answer.
• Offer only genuine options; use one clear sentence.

MIND BEND
A belief that works only under certain conditions is not a law; context turns absolutes back into local rules.

FORMULA FLOW
Name The Belief → Imagine Four Limits → Test Inside → Test Outside → Shrink the Rule

SAFETY
PAUSE
Do not use belief boundaries to minimise abuse, discrimination, medical facts, legal duties, or immediate danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

• Estimate honestly; cut what cannot fit.

ritualText:
END, THEN MOVE

PLAY TIME
60–120 seconds

GOAL
Choose the exact stopping point, perform one closing action, and physically leave.

HOW TO PLAY
1. Spot Pull — Name the exact point where the task is allowed to stop.
2. Store Handoff — Notice what your mind predicts will happen if you leave it unfinished.
3. Stop Clean — Choose one visible closing action.
4. Shift Body — Do the closing action and step away.
5. Check Result — Leave the remaining work for the next planned return point.

WIN
The task stopped at the planned edge, with remaining work assigned to the next return.

• Check the clock; name where to resume.
• Protect the next commitment; decide the finish point first.
• Close the file; choose finish point.
• Keep water within reach; say where to resume next.
• Check hunger and time; do not add one more thing.

MIND BEND
Stopping feels dangerous when the mind equates unfinished with lost. A visible closure action proves the work can remain incomplete without remaining active.

FORMULA FLOW
Spot Pull → Store Handoff → Stop Clean → Shift Body → Check Result

SAFETY
PAUSE
Stop if this makes you less steady, more distressed, or less able to act safely. Use human, professional, medical, or emergency support when the situation needs more than self-help.
This brief reset is not diagnosis, treatment, or emergency care.

title: BRIDGE RELAY
goal: Open the conversation with one sentence and let the other person finish before preparing your next move.
steps:
1. Name Difference — Separate the feeling from its command.
2. Take Action — Complete the opening sentence.
3. Hear Reply — Let the other person finish once.
win: The feeling lost command status, your opening landed, and one complete reply was actually heard.

• Avoid guessing their intent; say the main point first.

• Ask what they understood; check the request.

title: HANDRAIL GREEN LIGHT

win: You reached a calmer place, used a safe physical anchor, and contacted someone who could stay with you.
supports:
• Loosen your shoulders; avoid repeated pulse checking.
• Reduce caffeine; keep movements gentle.
• Reduce extra stimulation; unclench your jaw.
• Keep your body supported; sip water if it helps.

safety:
PAUSE

supports:

HOW TO PLAY
1. See Edges — State where you are right now.
2. Notice Wave — Notice the current body signal.
3. Slow Hands — Notice how fast your hands are moving and slow them one notch.
4. Change Place — Step once away from the cue.
5. Stay Connected — Move toward or contact the chosen support person.

WIN
You located yourself, slowed your hands, created distance from the cue, and moved toward support.

• Let breaths happen; avoid symptom searching.
• Stay somewhere physically safe; use ordinary surroundings.
• Seek care for new severe symptoms; stop body scanning.
• Loosen your shoulders; unclench your jaw.
• Avoid repeated pulse checking; sit somewhere safe.

MIND BEND
When attention narrows around a sensation, even neutral changes can look like confirmation. Widening the frame restores information the alarm was excluding.

FORMULA FLOW
See Edges → Notice Wave → Slow Hands → Change Place → Stay Connected

SAFETY
PAUSE
Keep your eyes open and orient to the room. Stop if symptoms intensify, you feel faint, or a medical problem may be possible. Call Triple Zero (000) for an emergency; otherwise use qualified medical advice. Do not induce or test symptoms.
This is brief self-help, not diagnosis or treatment.

title: THE HANDRAIL CHECK
goal: Respond to a frightening body sensation by orienting outward and moving toward safety.
steps:
1. Look Around — Notice one danger signal.
2. Name Signal — Name the current physical signal.
3. Cross Room — Move one step across space.
4. Move Someone — Move toward someone safe nearby.
win: A danger signal was noticed without becoming a verdict, and physical movement carried you toward someone safe.
supports:
• Let breaths happen; use ordinary surroundings.
• Keep movements gentle; unclench your jaw and shoulders.
• Reduce caffeine; stop body scanning.
• Sip water if it helps; look at ordinary objects nearby.
• Reduce extra stimulation; give the surge time to pass.
formula_flow: Look Around → Name Signal → Cross Room → Move Someone
safety:
PAUSE
Keep your eyes open and orient to the room. Stop if symptoms intensify, you feel faint, or a medical problem may be possible. Call Triple Zero (000) for an emergency; otherwise use qualified medical advice. Do not induce or test symptoms.
This is brief self-help, not diagnosis or treatment.

goal: Leave immediate hazards and let another person help slow a level of activation you cannot safely manage alone.
steps:
1. Exit Risk Area — Step away from traffic, heights, weapons, substances, or conflict.

3. Tell Safe Human — Tell someone clearly that you cannot slow down safely.
4. Contact Urgent Help — Use emergency or crisis support from the Safety section.
5. Wait With Support — Remain with support until the activation is professionally assessed.
win: You reached a lower-risk setting and remained with support until professional assessment began.

• Keep a trusted person with you.
• Avoid driving or risky decisions.
• Reduce caffeine and other stimulants.

title: FACT, TAP
goal: Interrupt a persistent loop with one fact, one step away, and one visible task.
steps:
1. Make Cue — Name one direct fact.
2. Set Aside — Take one step out of the pressure.
3. Close Loop — Return to one visible task.
win: The loop lost the whole field when a direct fact led back to something concrete.
supports:
• Use a short timer; set a clear stopping point.
• Avoid replaying the same evidence; leave unsolved questions.
• Limit how long you review it; ask for new information.
• Return to one physical task; use your hands.
• Stop repeated review; name one useful action.
formula_flow: Make Cue → Set Aside → Close Loop
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if this makes you less steady, more distressed, or less able to act safely. Use human, professional, medical, or emergency support when the situation needs more than self-help.
This brief reset is not diagnosis, treatment, or emergency care.
